feat: default modelContextLimit capped at 150K

Pi models often have 1M context windows, but in practice 150K is enough
for most coding sessions. Capping the effective limit at 150K makes
compression much more aggressive:

Before (1M limit):  growth threshold 50K, emergency at 800K
After (150K limit):  growth threshold 20K, emergency at 120K

Pi status bar still shows the real model context window (1M).
ACP manages a tighter working set within that window.

Override via ACP_MODEL_CONTEXT_LIMIT env var or adapter config.

fix: modelContextLimit reflects model context window, not a 150K cap

Commit 4239962 introduced DEFAULT_TARGET=150_000 and Math.min(live, 150K),
forcing every model's effective context limit down to 150K regardless of its
real context window. This is wrong because modelContextLimit is the denominator
that drives ALL of acp-kernel's thresholds, and acp-kernel already derives them
as ratios of that limit:

  - truncate.threshold   = 1.0  x modelContextLimit  -> 150K models would
    start TRUNCATING messages (not compressing) at 150K
  - nudge.maxContextLimitPct = 0.55 x limit
  - nudge.emergencyThresholdPct = 0.8 x limit
  - growthFloor = max(20000, round(limit * 0.05)), capped by growthCap=50000

Capping the denominator silently corrupts every downstream threshold and makes
the kernel believe the model only has 150K of context.

The commit message's intent ("make compression more aggressive on 1M models")
has dedicated knobs for exactly this: coreOverrides -> nudge.growthCap /
nudge.maxContextLimitPct / nudge.emergencyThresholdPct, already exposed via
AdapterConfig.coreOverrides. Use those instead of mutating the limit.

Fix: drop the Math.min cap. modelContextLimit now truthfully reflects the
model's context window (liveContextLimit), read from ctx.model.contextWindow.
150K is kept ONLY as a fallback when the window is unavailable (live=0).

Priority: env ACP_MODEL_CONTEXT_LIMIT > adapter.modelContextLimit
         > live model contextWindow > 150K fallback.

Added tests/config.test.ts covering all branches and the no-cap regression.

fix: inline typebox into dist (was crashing extension load, no tags/nudge)

tsup.config.ts listed "typebox" in `external`, so dist/index.js kept four
runtime `import { Type } from "typebox"` statements. But pai-acp's
package.json has NO dependencies (typebox is a transitive dep of
@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent), and the pi install layout
(~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/) does NOT contain typebox at any level.
Result: at session start, `import "typebox"` threw ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND,
the extension's module evaluation crashed, and pi silently dropped it —
so the `context` event handler never registered, meaning NO ref-tag
injection and NO nudge, even though the acp_status tool still worked
(loaded via a separate path). ACP compression effectively disappeared.

Remove "typebox" from `external` and add it to `noExternal` to force
esbuild to bundle it (typebox is ESM-only with no `main`, which is why
tsup left it external by default). dist grows 123KB→330KB (now carries
the typebox runtime inline); verified zero `from "typebox"` remain and
that the dist loads cleanly in an environment with NO typebox installed
(context handler registers, 4 tools + 4 commands).

This is a Blocker-class regression: every pai-acp install that ran under
a pi layout without a resolvable typebox had silent context-management
failure. Likely introduced when tool schemas started importing Type.

fix: record compressCallId so consumed compress calls get hidden

compress-tool ignored the execute() toolCallId parameter (it was
prefixed `_`). applyCompression never received compressCallId, so every
created block had compressCallId === undefined. As a result
hideConsumedCompressCalls saw an empty allBlockCallIds set: successful
compress calls were indistinguishable from failed ones, all treated as
orphans, and only the last 2 were kept — the rest (including stale
failed attempts like error messages) stayed in context permanently.

Fix: pass toolCallId through execute → handleCompress →
applyCompression.ranges[].compressCallId. Now a successful compress
records the toolCallId on its block, and hideConsumedCompressCalls can
match it to hide the consumed tool-call + tool-result pair.

Also bump acp-kernel dependency 0.0.7 → 0.0.9 (tokenizer fix, unified
tier model, range list, reason fix all landed there).

refactor: decompress switches to append semantics (no deactivate)

Problem: decompress called deactivateBlock, which un-folded the block's
messages IN PLACE. That mutated the message array mid-prefix → cache
miss for everything after the block. Worse, the next turn's syncBlocks
fork-recovery re-activated the block (messages still present), silently
undoing the decompress. The tool ALSO returned a truncated preview at
the end, so content was duplicated (in-place + trailing preview).

New behavior (append semantics):
- decompress does NOT call deactivateBlock and does NOT save state.
- The block stays compressed (folded); its summary stays in place.
- Full content is collected and returned as the tool result, which the
  host appends to the conversation naturally (at the attention focus).
- Cache prefix is preserved (message array unchanged except the appended
  tool result). syncBlocks conflict disappears (active never changes).
- Idempotent: repeated calls return the content again (block stays
  active; no "already inactive" state to get stuck on).

full:false → one tier up (nested active children stay folded, their
summaries shown; block's direct messages in full).
full:true  → recurse through all nested tiers to original messages.

Applies to both the decompress tool and the /acp-decompress command.

Previously, the parent chain walk only triggered on ENOENT (file missing).

feat: auto-retry provider token rate-limit errors (Bedrock throttle) with progressive backoff

Detects provider-side per-minute token throttling — e.g. AWS Bedrock's
"Too many tokens, please wait before trying again." relayed through an
OpenAI-compatible endpoint as content + finish_reason "error_finish"
(surface: 'Provider finish_reason: error_finish') — which previously
failed the turn immediately (matches neither pi's overflow nor retry
patterns).

Design (hybrid, per design review):
- message_end: rewrite the finalized error's errorMessage to a
  pi-recognizable 429 form so pi's NATIVE retry re-runs the same turn
  (no duplicate user message, error kept out of LLM context, native
  TUI indicator). pi's native budget is small/fast (3x, 2s base).
- agent_settled: when a run still ends on the throttle error and the
  ACP budget allows, wait a progressive delay (default 60s, x2 per
  kick, capped 5min) then send one auto-marked user message
  ([ACP:provider-throttle] ...) to resume the interrupted step.
- input: any new user input cancels a pending kick.
- episode budget: maxRetries (default 10) ACP-driven retries per error
  episode; any non-error response or new user message resets.
- config: throttleRetry (boolean | { enabled, maxRetries, baseDelayMs,
  maxDelayMs, backoffMode }) via acp.json, defaults
  true/10/60000/300000/exponential; false restores fail-fast.

Deliberately NOT retried (fail-fast preserved): real context-overflow
errors, quota/billing exhaustion, generic 429s.

feat: self-heal context window on upstream overflow (extension side)

When the model API rejects a request because the context is too large
(a context-overflow 400), the extension now reacts on the next turn:

1. LEARN the real window: many providers state it in the error body
   ("prompt is too long: ... > 128000 maximum", "maximum context length is
   128000 tokens"). It is persisted per-session and the kernel's nudge/
   truncate bands are re-centered on it — below the real limit, not above
   it (the 150k fallback puts those bands above a smaller real window, so
   nothing fires before the overflow).
2. ARM an emergency: the next context event's usage is forced to >=95% so
   the kernel's emergency nudge + tool-result truncate fire immediately,
   even if the density-calibrated estimate under-reports the sent view.

This is the extension-side mirror of the proxy's overflow self-heal
(billion-context PR #172). Unlike throttle-retry it does NOT rewrite the
error or ask pi to retry: the overflow is real, and re-sending the same
context would overflow again. The error surfaces; the next turn recovers.

  (pure detection + window parsing) + OverflowEpisode (per-session state).
- src/runtime.ts: per-session overflowFor(sid) (a Map, like the throttle
  episode pattern).
- src/index.ts: wireOverflowSelfHeal (message_end detects + arms; the
  context handler re-centers the learned window + applies the armed boost,
  which feeds processTurn only — density.update uses the raw sentTokens so
  calibration is untouched).
- tests/overflow-selfheal.test.ts (new): 12 unit tests (detection, window
  parsing, Bedrock-throttle/quota negatives, sub-1000 floor, episode).

fix(compress): break dead-range compress loops; add enabled master switch (closes #250)

Small local models (e.g. quantized 27B) loop on identical compress calls
with refs that can never resolve (stale/consumed or unknown): the kernel
rejects every time and the model retries the same dead refs for minutes.
The existing per-turn cap only suppressed nudge re-injection, not the
tool itself, and the kernel's 'run acp_status' hint is unexecutable for
small models.

1. Dead-range repeat breaker: the compress tool pre-checks every
   requested range against the kernel's boundary-resolver semantics
   (unknown ref, consumed-without-active-owner). After 2 identical
   all-dead failures it returns a hard rejection listing the LIVE
   compressible ranges (from the nudge decision computed in the same
   call) instead of the kernel's stale-refs error. The rejection keeps
   the 0-block panel shape so it still counts toward the per-turn cap.
2. Turn-cap tool enforcement: once MAX_COMPRESS_ATTEMPTS failed/no-op
   outcomes burn in one user turn, every further compress call for that
   turn is rejected (PAUSED) until the next user message — including
   calls with live refs.
3. enabled:false master switch (adapter config or acp.json, project
   overrides global): registers nothing — no tools, no system prompt,
   no context transform, no compaction-cancel — leaving Pi's native
   context management in control for models too small to drive ACP.

fix(#453): latch compress-retry cap under fork hosts via persisted-boundary key

Under non-pi hosts (PI_ACP_FORK_HOST) the context handler's entries include
the live-merged tail, whose unpersisted user message carries a volatile
live-N id that renumbers on every fire (its own prior ref blocks the base
candidate in nextLiveId). The retry breaker keyed on that boundary id, so
failTurnKey churned mid-episode: noteCompressOutcomes reset failCount on
each key change and compressRetryCappedFor's exact-equality check failed on
the next fire — the cap never latched and emergency-inject resumed right
after every 'compress-retry-capped failures=3'.

Key both retry-tracking consumers (transform-side outcome collection +
cap check, tool-side PAUSED rejection) to a new stable key derived from
persisted entries only (retryBreakerKey). Persisted ids are immutable, so
the cap now holds until a successful compress, a genuinely new persisted
user message, or session lifecycle clear. Pi-native hosts see no behavior
change (persisted view == merged view there). Nudge-shown dedup/growth
stamps keep the merged-view key (separate concern).

Adds tests/compress-retry-fork-host.test.ts: unit test for retryBreakerKey
plus an end-to-end fork-host scenario reproducing the #452 log pattern
(cap latches through live-id churn; new persisted user message releases).

fix(#325): floor meter at provider anchor minus tokens reclaimed since it

After a successful compress, usageAnchorPredatesCompression() skipped the
provider-usage floor entirely, so tokenCount fell back to the raw sent-view
estimate — which structurally omits tool-definition schemas, ref-tag overhead,
and the injected nudge (a fixed ~70–80K for this host). The meter read
false-idle; on the next turn a fresh provider usage re-engaged the floor at the
full real prompt size (~84–95% of limit) and fired a spurious EMERGENCY, which
the model answered by compressing again → loop.

Fix: when the anchor predates a successful compress, floor at
(lastProviderUsage − netReclaimedSinceAnchor) instead of skipping. netReclaimed
sums max(0, compressedTokens − summaryTokens) over active blocks whose creating
compress toolResult lands after the last valid usage anchor. The provider's
real number already counts all fixed overhead accurately, so subtracting only
the genuinely-freed tokens yields an exact post-compression size without needing
to measure tool schemas (unmeasurable/unstable in the extension). New work added
after the compress still grows tokenCount via sentTokens as before.

that reclaimed little still correctly trips the nudge.
